inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR statement of changes in equity: equity-settled share-based payments GBP2m (FY2024: GBP1m); plus GBP3m cash 'Melrose equity-settled compensation scheme related payments' in the FY2025 FCF reconciliation (employer taxes on the matured 2020 plan). FY2026 guidance: GBP3m non-cash LTIP charge.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence sterling (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts a GBP-per-share value to pence. No FX market rate involved and nothing to re-date; the 1,248m share count divides GBP millions to GBP per share before the x100. Parity check: adjusted diluted EPS 32.1p FY2025 against GBP410m adjusted profit after tax / 1,276m weighted diluted shares = GBP0.321 = 32.1p.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,246m ordinary shares in issue excluding treasury at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 interim) plus c.2m dilutive shares from the Melrose equity-settled share plans (diluted weighted 1,252m vs basic 1,250m). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows (tiny, GBP3m/yr), and the GBP175m buyback is paused pending Garden Grove, so no buyback shrinkage is assumed either.
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP flows, GBP discount rate. UK 10y gilt c.4.5% + 5.0% ERP x beta c.1.15 (levered aerospace tier-1, 1.8x covenant leverage) = cost of equity c.10.25%; cost of debt 5.3% pre-tax (company guidance on drawn debt) = c.4.0% after tax; D/(D+E) c.22% at the current price -> WACC c.8.9%, rounded to 9.0%. The same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, customer concentration and the Garden Grove tail are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Lease principal (GBP31m FY2025) plus lease interest (GBP12m FY2025) = GBP43m = 1.2% of revenue is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (1.3% going forward, consistent with FY2026 guidance of c.GBP40m leased-asset depreciation and c.GBP14m lease interest). Lease liabilities (GBP323m at 30 June 2026) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt, which matches the company's own net debt definition (interest-bearing loans and borrowings less cash). D&A for cash-tax EBIT is owned-asset D&A only (FY2025: GBP138m total less GBP31m right-of-use depreciation = GBP107m = 3.0%; FY2026 guidance c.GBP110m).
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest (nil on the FY2024/FY2025 balance sheets after the Dowlais demerger). Flows are 100% attributable; no bridge deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating industrial; dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the adaptations file applied: GBP-built WACC, single lease treatment, GBp quote). FY0 is FY2025, the second full Aerospace-only year after the April 2023 Dowlais demerger; the pre-demerger FY2015-FY2022 multi-division history in the Metrics CSV is not the business being valued and is not used for projections (the FY2022 Aerospace-only restatement, revenue GBP2,954m, lives in kpis). KEY MODELLING CHOICE - RRSP cash conversion: adjusted operating profit (GBP647m) converts to only GBP125m of free cash flow because engine RRSP variable consideration is recognised as revenue at OE delivery while the cash arrives over decades of aftermarket ('unbilled work done' build GBP324m FY2025, GBP274m FY2024, c.GBP316m implied by FY2026 guidance), plus GTF powder-metal (PMI) payments (GBP68m FY2025, c.GBP50m 2026, c.GBP200m total) and GBP20m/yr pension contributions. The engine has a single scalar wc_capture, so this time-varying programme investment is carried in capex_pct_path = pure capex (3.4% FY2026 guidance GBP120-140m, easing to 3.0%) + unbilled/RRSP build + PMI + pension, and is decayed as the RRSP portfolio turns cash-positive (management: all 19 RRSPs cash-positive in 2028). ebitda_margin_path is therefore management's adjusted EBITDA margin (post-IFRS 16, FY2025 21.9%) so it ties to the reported series. wc_capture_pct of -10% covers ordinary inventory/receivables growth ex-factoring. FACTORING: the GBP396m non-recourse factoring book is excluded from net debt (true sale, outside the covenant definition) AND the guided GBP30-50m/yr factoring inflow is excluded from the flows - the stock is charged nowhere and the flow is credited nowhere. CASH TAX: cash tax was GBP12m (2.3% of adjusted PBT) in FY2025 and c.4% guided for 2026 because of GBP530m of deferred tax assets on losses; that shelter is NOT perpetuated - the cash rate on EBIT ramps 4% -> 24% blended statutory (UK 25%, US c.25%, Sweden 20.6%, NL 25.8%) over six years. BUYBACKS: GBP173m repurchased in FY2025 and GBP250m programme completed March 2026, so the flat count has historically been funded; the GBP175m programme is paused since June 2026. Garden Grove is carried as an explicit equity-bridge deduction, not in the flows. Y1 (FY2026) is calibrated to the maintained guidance (revenue GBP3.75-3.95bn, adjusted operating profit GBP700-750m, FCF GBP150-200m incl. factoring) less c.GBP35m revenue / c.GBP15m profit of Garden Grove throughput loss; the base Y1 build gives c.GBP265m unlevered owner FCF, i.e. c.GBP135m after c.GBP130m cash interest, which sits inside guidance once the GBP30-50m factoring inflow is removed. last_fcf is the company-defined FCF (after interest and tax, after lease principal) less SBC and legacy-plan cash; it is a levered anchor and is not the engine's FY0 flow.

equity_bridge.item: Garden Grove incident: up to $100m claims programme (c.GBP75m) plus GBP25-30m H2 2026 exceptional costs, no insurance recovery assumed
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 interim: contingent liabilities note and outlook; August 2026 claims programme announcement. Litigation and regulatory penalties beyond this are unquantified and sit in the bear weight.

equity_bridge.item: Government refundable advances (debt-like, repaid from programme sales)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr on the Aerospace-only basis: FY2022 restated GBP2,954m (kpis RevenueRestatedPostDemerger) to FY2025 GBP3,589m
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity, EPS and FCF CAGRs are not computable on a like-for-like basis: the April 2023 demerger removed Automotive/Powder Metallurgy (FY2022 group revenue GBP7,537m vs GBP2,954m Aerospace-only), shares were consolidated 3-for-1, FY2023 net income carries the GBP1,020m demerger loss, book equity fell 21% FY2023-FY2025 purely from GBP697m of buybacks and dividends, and owner FCF was negative in FY2023 and FY2024 (first positive year FY2025). Adjusted diluted EPS 18.7p -> 32.1p (FY2023-FY2025, +31%/yr) and adjusted operating profit GBP147m -> GBP647m (FY2022 restated to FY2025) are margin-recovery rates, not sustainable growth; the 6.7% revenue CAGR is the only series that describes the business being valued.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (company FCF less SBC): FY2023 c.-GBP118m (CSV -113 less SBC 5), FY2024 -GBP75m (company -74 less SBC 1; CSV -244 includes the GBP198m cash settlement of the 2020 incentive plan), FY2025 GBP120m. No CAGR exists from a negative base; the FY2024->FY2025 swing was GBP195m, of which GBP95m lower restructuring cash.

base.narrative: Base: OE ramp delivers high-single-digit growth to 2028 then decelerates; EBITDA margin reaches 25.5% in 2029 (adjusted operating margin c.21.5%, below the 24%+ target); RRSP cash conversion improves but more slowly than management's 2028 cash-positive milestone implies, giving c.GBP400m FCF after interest in 2029 against the GBP600m target.

bull.narrative: Bull: management's 2029 targets are met - c.GBP5bn revenue, 24%+ adjusted operating margin, all 19 RRSPs cash-positive in 2028 so the unbilled build halves by 2029 and FCF approaches GBP600m; defence (NATO 3.5% pathway) and additive/repair wins extend growth into the 2030s.

bear.narrative: Bear: forgings/castings/powder shortages and OEM build-rate slips cap growth at low-single digits, Airframes stays a 6-7% margin business so Group EBITDA margin stalls near 23%, RRSP cash conversion lags (shop-visit timing, further PMI-type programme costs) so the unbilled drag stays above 5% of revenue for a decade, and Garden Grove litigation/regulatory costs run past the claims programme.

scenario_narratives.base: The OE ramp (A320neo to 70-75/month by end-2027, 737 MAX, 787) and a maturing GTF/GEnx/XWB aftermarket carry revenue at 7-8% through 2028 before decelerating to 2.5%; adjusted EBITDA margin rises from 21.9% to 26.5% (operating margin to c.22%, short of the 24%+ target) as Engines mix grows and Brilliant Basics lifts Airframes. The decisive variable is cash conversion: the RRSP unbilled build (c.8% of revenue today) decays to c.3% by the mid-2030s, so owner FCF rises from c.GBP265m unlevered in FY2026 to c.GBP500m in 2029 - roughly two-thirds of management's GBP600m post-interest target. Cash tax normalises to 24% as the GBP530m loss DTA is consumed. Garden Grove costs GBP100m in the bridge and nothing more.
scenario_narratives.bull: Management's 2029 framework is delivered at constant currency: c.GBP5bn revenue, 24%+ operating margin (Engines mid-to-high 30s), and the whole RRSP portfolio cash-positive in 2028 so the unbilled build halves and FCF approaches GBP600m. NATO's 3.5%-of-GDP pathway, uncrewed-platform wins (NYX, Brontanax, FMV) and additive/repair contracts with all three engine OEMs extend high-single-digit growth into the 2030s; the buyback restarts in 2027 as leverage falls below 1.5x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Supply-chain constraints and OEM rate slips hold growth at 3-4%; a civil-demand shock (Middle East conflict, fuel prices) delays shop visits so RRSP aftermarket cash lags the accounting revenue, keeping the unbilled drag above 5% of revenue for a decade; Airframes remains structurally 6-7% margin; the Garden Grove legal and regulatory tail (30+ civil suits, federal/state investigations) runs beyond the $100m claims programme; leverage stays near 2x, the buyback remains paused, and a 14x terminal cap applies to a business that never demonstrates the cash conversion the equity story depends on.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear weight raised because the thesis rests on an unproven pivot in cash conversion (FY2025 was the first positive-FCF year; adjusted profit converts at under 40%), there is a live, unquantified legal and regulatory tail from Garden Grove, leverage is 1.8x with a further GBP396m of factoring, and the business depends on five OEM customers. Bull weight cut because the bull case needs several independent things to go right at once: OE build rates, supply-chain unblocking, Airframes margin repair and the 2028 RRSP cash-positive milestone.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Melrose is valued as a long-duration engine-aftermarket annuity wrapped in a lower-margin aerostructures business. Because IFRS 15 front-loads RRSP revenue, reported adjusted profit overstates current cash generation by roughly GBP300m a year; the valuation therefore keys off owner free cash flow built from components, with the RRSP programme investment carried explicitly and decayed, cash tax normalised rather than the loss shelter perpetuated, leases charged once as an operating cost, and factoring credited nowhere. Management's 2029 targets define the bull case, not the base. Risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights at a single 9% GBP WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: RRSP cash conversion: if the unbilled-work-done build does not decay as modelled, the terminal FCF margin (c.11% of revenue in base) is overstated; each 1pp of permanent drag is worth roughly GBP0.5bn of enterprise value.
Garden Grove: the GBP100m bridge covers the claims programme and H2 exceptionals only; civil litigation and regulatory penalties are unquantified.
Customer and programme concentration on Airbus, Boeing, Pratt & Whitney, GE and Rolls-Royce; GTF-type programme costs (PMI c.GBP200m) can recur.
Cash-tax normalisation timing: the GBP530m loss DTA could last longer (value upside) or be curtailed by jurisdiction mismatch (downside).
FX: c.70% of revenue is USD/EUR against GBP reporting; a 1 cent GBP/USD move is c.GBP5m of operating profit.
Terminal value is c.70% of enterprise value at a 9% WACC and 2.5% growth; the required-return table shows the steepness.
